evidence.excerpt:
Long-horizon embodied agents face temporal confusion and incomplete or distorted records,
recurring errors from fixed memory rules, and growing storage and retrieval costs. We present
BetaMem, a framework for building and evolving traceable long-term memory through six linked
layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural memory. A dual-level write
contract constrains operation executability and source support for content: supervised fine-tuning
learns compliant memory operations, while reinforcement learning combines repeated sampling with
teacher verification of the original observations to reward complete, accurate records and penalize
omissions, distortion, and unsupported content. We formulate failure-driven policy recursive self-
improvement through diagnosis along the causal sequence of memory operations and local rule
repairs gated by independent

retaining every observation consumes substantial storage and read resources. Memory operations
must balance their expected answer value against these costs [31].
To address these challenges, we proposeBetaMem, an evidence-grounded world-memory framework for
long-horizon embodied agents. First, the framework organizes observations and experience into six linked
memory layers (L0–L5): L0 working memory holds current observations and task state; L1 spatial, L2
entity, and L3 episodic memory link places, people and objects, and event histories; and L4 experiential
and L5 procedural memory retain regularities and reusable procedures supported across experiences. The
layers record observation time, validity interval, and revision time, while adual-level write contract

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline gains are measured on external benchmarks with ground-truth exact match, simulator success/error recurrence, and external judge protocols, which are materially independent of the teacher-verified GRPO write signal and the RSI regression sets.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External benchmark protocols: M3-Bench judged accuracy, LoCoMo Mem0-protocol LLM judge, OpenEQA LLM-Match, EgoLifeQA four-choice exact match, and EMem-Bench simulator success and error recurrence.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GRPO optimizes memory writes against deterministic contract checks and qwen3.7-max teacher replay of original frames; failure-driven RSI selects rule repairs on a held-out regression set.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics directly match the tabular evidence, supporting claims of improved accuracy, lower error recurrence, and enhanced generation efficiency using a 9B model.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is comprehensively evaluated across four established long-horizon question-answering benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot, LoCoMo, OpenEQA EM-EQA, EgoLifeQA) and the interactive EMem-Bench, demonstrating clear improvements over prior systems alongside detailed ablation and efficiency studies.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance is corroborated across multiple independent benchmarks using varied external metrics including ground-truth exact match and simulator execution success.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark test suites evaluated via external LLM judges (Mem0 protocol on LoCoMo, LLM-Match on OpenEQA), exact-match multiple-choice QA (EgoLifeQA), benchmark QA protocols (M3-Bench), and task simulator success/error recurrence (EMem-Bench).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GRPO training optimizes memory writes via deterministic rule checks and qwen3.7-max teacher verification against original observation frames, while failure-driven RSI optimizes memory rules on regression validation sets.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including failure modes in joint visual/map alignment, validator-proposer bias, potential degradation under distribution shift, and privacy implications of person-linked memories.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying the six memory layers, a dual-level contract distinguishing interface from content validity, objective functions for RL write-learning, and an algorithmic loop for policy repair and replay.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a substantial, well-formulated architectural contribution to embodied agent memory with sound methodological constraints, strong experimental comparisons on recognized standard benchmarks, and honest discussions of system boundaries.
primary.scoped_contribution: BetaMem introduces a six-layer, evidence-grounded long-term memory framework for embodied agents that combines dual-level contract-based write learning (SFT and GRPO with teacher verification) and failure-driven recursive policy self-improvement under explicit resource budgets.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper presents a substantial, well-formulated architectural contribution to embodied agent memory with sound methodological constraints, strong experimental comparisons on recognized standard benchmarks, and honest discussions of system boundaries.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including failure modes in joint visual/map alignment, validator-proposer bias, potential degradation under distribution shift, and privacy implications of person-linked memories.
